installation.note: history is a built-in shell command available in bash and most shells

overview.summary: history displays the command history - a list of previously executed commands. This is a built-in shell command (not a separate program) that helps you recall and reuse previous commands. You can search, repeat, or edit previous commands using history.
when_to_use: Find a command you used before
Search for specific commands in history

syntax.description: Display command history. If N is specified, show last N commands. Without arguments, shows all history.

options.use_case: Erase all command history (use with caution)
Remove a specific command from history

options.description: Write current history to history file
options.use_case: Save current session history to file immediately

misconceptions.title: history shows all commands ever
misconceptions.misconception: history displays all commands from all sessions
misconceptions.reality: history shows commands from current session and saved history. History is limited by HISTSIZE setting (usually 1000-5000 commands). Old commands are truncated.
misconceptions.tip: History is limited - check HISTSIZE. Old commands are removed when limit is reached.

misconceptions.title: history is a separate program
misconceptions.misconception: history is an external command like ls or cat
misconceptions.reality: history is a built-in shell command (part of bash). This is why 'which history' may show nothing or an alias.
misconceptions.tip: history is built into the shell - it's not a separate program you can call directly.

common_pitfalls.description: Using history -c clears all history permanently
common_pitfalls.solution: Be careful with history -c - it clears history immediately. History is usually saved automatically on logout.

common_pitfalls.description: Commands from one terminal session don't appear in another
common_pitfalls.solution: History saves on logout. Use history -w to save immediately. Check HISTFILE and HISTSIZE settings.

common_pitfalls.description: Mistyping history number and executing wrong command
common_pitfalls.solution: Verify history number with history first. Or use Ctrl+R for interactive history search (safer).

related_commands.relationship: Edit and repeat history; more advanced than history
related_commands.description: Edit and re-execute previous commands (more advanced than !number)

best_practices: Use Ctrl+R for interactive history search (safer than !number)
Pipe history to less for long output: history | less
Search history: history | grep keyword to find commands
Use history 20 to see recent commands only
Use !! to repeat last command (very common pattern)
Use !number carefully - verify the command before executing
Use history -d to remove specific commands from history if needed
performance_tips: history is fast even with large history lists
Use history 20 or similar to limit output if history is long
Searching with grep is efficient: history | grep keyword

additional_notes.builtin: history is a built-in shell command, not a separate program
additional_notes.history_file: History is saved to ~/.bash_history (bash) or similar for other shells
additional_notes.size_limit: History size is limited by HISTSIZE environment variable (usually 1000-5000)
additional_notes.interactive_search: Use Ctrl+R for interactive reverse search through history (easier than !number)
additional_notes.repeat_patterns: Common: !! (last command), !-1 (same as !!), !-2 (second to last), !string (last command starting with string)
